title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. V is a discrete valuation ring, which may be assumed complete. The text writes S = Spec V without defining S. V has perfect residue field k of characteristic p > 0 and fraction field K of characteristic 0 or p. The objects are p-Barsotti–Tate groups (p-divisible groups) M = (M(ν))_{ν≥0} over K.

Condition de monodromie. M satisfies the monodromy condition if it has a composition series by sub-BT groups whose graded pieces N = Gr^i(M) have 'essentially good reduction'. This means that after some finite separable extension K'/K, N_{K'} extends to a BT group over the normalization S' of S in K'. In modern terms the graded pieces are potentially good (potentially crystalline / potentially Barsotti–Tate). M itself is then a successive extension of such pieces. This is the p-divisible-group analogue of potentially semistable reduction. The model case is the Tate curve: 0 → μ_{p^∞} → E[p^∞] → Q_p/Z_p → 0.

Uniqueness and descent data. By Tate's theorem, the generic-fibre functor BT(S') → BT(K') is fully faithful. The typed text says this is known only in equal characteristic; Grothendieck corrects it by hand to 'inégales', which is correct since Tate 1967 assumes char K = 0. So the model N over S' is unique up to unique isomorphism. If K'/K is Galois with group G, transport of structure gives a semilinear G-action on N, compatible with the action on S'. One K' can serve for all i (take the compositum); such a K' is called a 'corps de bonne réduction virtuelle' for M.

Grothendieck-group packaging. K_BT(K;K') is the Grothendieck group of BT groups over K having K' as a field of virtual good reduction. Map (1) is K_BT(K;K') → K_BT(S';G), the Grothendieck group of BT groups over S' with semilinear G-action. Since S is henselian, S' is local, which sets up the next step.

Continuation on the next page. (2) restricts to the closed point s'. (3) applies the covariant Dieudonné functor BT(k') → free W(k')-modules (≃ crystals), equivariantly for G. Restricting to the inertia subgroup I (which acts trivially on k', hence W(k')-linearly) gives R_{W(k')}(I)^{G/I}. Taking traces then gives a G-invariant W(k')-valued class function on I: the 'caractère' of M.

This character is independent of K' and is viewed as a function on the (infinite) inertia group of Gal(K̄/K). It is a p-adic, crystalline analogue of the Serre–Tate inertial character of an abelian variety with potentially good reduction. It is essentially what was later called the inertial type of a potentially Barsotti–Tate representation, defined through the Dieudonné module of the descended reduction.
errors: S is used ('normalisé S' de S', 'S étant complet') but never defined; it must be Spec V.

The typed attribution of Tate's theorem to 'égales caractéristiques' is wrong; Grothendieck's handwritten correction 'inégales' is right. Tate (1967) requires char K = 0. The equal-characteristic full faithfulness was proved only by de Jong (Invent. Math. 1998).

Gap: for (1) to be well defined on Grothendieck groups, an exact sequence of potentially-good BT groups over K' must extend to an exact sequence over S'. In mixed characteristic this follows from Tate's results (schematic closure of a generic sub-BT group is BT), but it is not stated. In equal characteristic it would need de Jong-type results.
Minor: the text says G acts on N; the action is semilinear (compatible with the action on S'), which the text does acknowledge, so N is not an S'-linear G-representation.

ideas.what: Condition de monodromie: a p-divisible group over a local field admits a filtration by BT subgroups whose graded pieces have potentially good reduction
ideas.modern_name: p-adic analogue of potentially semistable reduction / p-adic monodromy (cf. Fontaine's p-adic monodromy conjecture, proved by Berger, André, Kedlaya, Mebkhout)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (l-adic monodromy theorem, SGA 7 IX); Fontaine for the p-adic formulation
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Grothendieck's ICM 1970 talk 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'; l-adic version in SGA 7 I/IX

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the good-reduction model via Tate's full faithfulness, giving canonical Galois descent data on the model over S'
ideas.modern_name: BT group with descent data / potentially Barsotti–Tate representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1967); descent-data formalism used by Conrad–Diamond–Taylor, Breuil (1990s)

ideas.what: Grothendieck groups K_BT(K;K') and K_BT(S';G) of BT groups with virtual good reduction, mapped to representation rings of inertia
Character of a BT group: trace of inertia acting on the Dieudonné module of the reduction of the good-reduction model, valued in W(k'), G-invariant
ideas.modern_name: inertial (Weil–Deligne) type of a potentially Barsotti–Tate / potentially crystalline representation, via D_pcris
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate 1968 (l-adic); Fontaine 1994 (p-adic, D_pst); Conrad–Diamond–Taylor 1999 and Breuil–Mézard 2002 (types of potentially BT reps)

missed.claim: Around 1969 Grothendieck defined the inertial character of a potentially good-reduction p-divisible group. He used the Dieudonné module of the reduction of the descended model, with its semilinear Gal(K'/K)-action restricted to inertia. This is essentially the inertial type of potentially Barsotti–Tate representations as used by Conrad–Diamond–Taylor and Breuil–Mézard 25–30 years later. It is usually traced to Fontaine's D_pst (1994), not to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: Soit K_BT(K;K') le groupe "de Grothendieck" défini par les groupes de BT sur K admettant K' comme corps de bonne réduction virtuelle ... K_BT(K;K') → K_BT(S';G)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the p-adic inertial type. It also suggests a K-theoretic (Grothendieck-group) formulation of types, including the equal-characteristic case, which is less studied.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly flags that the construction in equal characteristic needs Tate's full-faithfulness theorem there. This was open until de Jong 1998. The equal-characteristic theory of characters/types of BT groups over k((t)) seems little developed.
missed.quote: d'après le th. de Tate (démontré pour l'instant seulement dans le cas d'inégales caractéristiques)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Equal-characteristic inertial types for p-divisible groups or F-crystals over k((t)) (e.g. via de Jong, Kedlaya) could be compared with l-adic and p-adic types; it is unclear this was systematically done.

missed.claim: The 'condition de monodromie' (a filtration with potentially-good graded pieces) is posed as a property of BT groups over K. This is a p-adic counterpart of the l-adic monodromy theorem, foreshadowing the p-adic monodromy problem later formulated by Fontaine.
missed.quote: On dit qu'un tel groupe satisfait à la condition de monodromie s'il admet une suite de composition par des groupes de B.T., telle que les Gr^i(M) aient essentiellement bonne réduction
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's early formulation of p-adic monodromy for BT groups, relevant to the history of the p-adic monodromy theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, early (c.1969) definition of the p-adic inertial character/type of potentially good p-divisible groups via Dieudonné modules with descent data, packaged in Grothendieck groups. It anticipates notions usually credited to Fontaine and CDT/Breuil–Mézard. It is a natural transposition of Serre–Tate, however, and may be partly reflected in Grothendieck's 1970 ICM talk.
